title: Service Stewardship: Rotations, Crisis Comms, and Postmortem Workflow
author: Priya Nandakumar
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood's operational guidance for service stewardship: how teams schedule and run on-call rotations, conduct fast triage, execute customer and status communications during incidents, and run the postmortem process with a bias for learning and closure. It is intended for primary responders, rotation leads, product owners, and the incident communications cadre.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-ack and time-to-stable for customer-impacting incidents.
- Provide clear ownership for every phase of an incident (detect, contain, restore, notify, learn).
- Standardize customer-facing communications to protect trust while avoiding premature technical statements.
- Ensure postmortems turn into concrete, tracked action items and that runbooks remain current.

Who this applies to
- Engineering responders (SRE, serving runtime, infra, platform)
- Customer Success for customer comms & severity alignment
- Product and Security for impacted product decisions and regulatory evidence

High-level incident lifecycle (one-line)
1) Signal received -> 2) Triage & classify severity -> 3) Contain & mitigate -> 4) Restore service -> 5) Customer & internal comms -> 6) Postmortem & follow-up

Severity definitions (team-canonical)
- Sev 1 (Critical): System-wide or multi-region outage with >50% of customers affected, immediate executive notification. Target: page within 3 minutes, first bridge in 10 minutes.
- Sev 2 (High): Major functionality degraded for a subset of customers or significant error-rate increase. Target: page within 10 minutes, bridge within 30 minutes.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Localized degradation with feature impact; handled by on-call with async updates.
- Sev 4 (Low): Non-customer-impacting alerts, maintenance tasks, or noise.

Ownership matrix (quick reference)
| Responsibility | Primary | Secondary | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pager handling & triage | Rotation responder | Rotation lead | Acknowledge within target 
| Bridge operator (status updates) | Rotation lead | Customer Success rep | Start bridge for Sev1/2
| Customer status drafts | Customer Success | Rotation lead | Use templates below
| Postmortem lead | Rotation lead | Product owner | Postmortem within 72 hours for Sev1/2

On-call rotation design
- Rotation length: standard is 1 week for SRE/serving-runtime primary rotation. Exceptions must be documented: long rotations (2+ weeks) require manager approval and backup schedule.
- Handoff window: 15-minute overlap at handoff for privileged roles (e.g., bridge operator, steward).
- Secondary (follow-the-sun): For multi-region coverage, primary rotates in region; secondary is on-call in next region to ensure 24h coverage.
- Time-off & fairness: Each engineer should have at least 4 weeks between hard-week rotations; rotation lead monitors load and can request swaps.

Creating a rotation entry (procedure)
1) Add entry in the oncall-schedule calendar (Team Schedules -> Redwood Oncall) with name, start/end, backup name, and contact methods.
2) Add runbook link to the calendar entry under "runbook_url" field.
3) Notify primary, secondary, and Customer Success via Slack #rotations and email 72 hours before start.
4) Rotation lead runs quick sanity check of runbook (smoke commands) within 48 hours prior.

Runbook hygiene & required sections
Every runbook must include the following sections and be validated annually:
- Overview and owner (team and person)
- Signal sources and alert thresholds
- Quick triage checklist (top 6 checks with commands)
- Containment steps (rate limiting, circuit-breakers, fallbacks)
- Restore steps (hotfix, rollback, scaling actions)
- Mitigation workarounds for customers
- Runbook test instructions (how to validate)
- Recent changes (changelog)
- Last test date and next review date

Quick triage checklist (copyable)
1) Confirm alert: identify metric/trace/trace-id and time window.
2) Check upstream dependencies (redis, kv-store, model-serving pool) via dashboards.
3) Determine blast radius: services, regions, tenant scope.
4) If blast radius > threshold, raise severity and call bridge.
5) Apply short-term containment (rate limit, disable feature flag).
6) Start thread for follow-up actions and evidence collection.

Bridge & comms play (immediate actions)
- Who to start bridge: rotation lead. If unavailable, primary responder starts.
- Bridge template: title, severity, time-of-detect, immediate impact, owner, link to runbook, next update ETA.
- Update cadence: every 15 minutes for Sev1; every 30 minutes for Sev2 until stable.

Status page templates
Public status page (short form)
- Title: [Region] Degraded API latency impacting customers
- Time detected: 2026-08-27T14:21 UTC
- Impact: Increased request latency for text-generation endpoints in us-west1. Some requests are timing out; retries may succeed.
- Current status: Engineers are investigating; mitigation in progress.
- Next update: 2026-08-27T14:40 UTC

Private customer notice (for affected customers)
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood inference latency (us-west1)
Body: Dear <Customer Name>,
We’re investigating elevated latency for the text-generation endpoints in us-west1 that may cause timeouts for some requests. Our SREs have applied temporary throttling and are rolling a mitigation across the cluster. We will provide our next update by <time>. If you see sustained errors, please reply to this thread or reach out to your CSM. We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

Escalation and executive notification
- Auto-escalation: Mute escalations for noise but ensure Sev1 triggers SMS to on-call, rotation lead, and the Pager Duty exec list.
- Exec brief: For Sev1 incidents lasting >30 minutes, rotation lead prepares a 4-line executive summary: (1) impact, (2) root cause hypothesis, (3) mitigation in place, (4) next steps and ETA.

Postmortem workflow (required for Sev1/2; recommended for Sevs 3 when customer impact is >1 tenant)
1) Triage owner publishes initial incident timeline in the incident doc within 24 hours.
2) Postmortem lead schedules the postmortem meeting within 72 hours (invited teams: engineering, product, customer success, security if applicable).
3) Draft postmortem sections: Summary, Impact, Timeline, Root cause analysis (5 whys / fishbone), Contributing factors, Corrective actions (owner + ETA), Preventative controls.
4) Action items are added to the central tracker (Jira project INF-OPS) with required SLA: one high/critical action within 2 weeks, others triaged into roadmap.
5) Postmortem must be published to the internal incident archive no later than 7 days after the incident and linked from the runbook.

Postmortem quality rubric (used by reviewer)
- Complete timeline with evidence (logs, traces, metrics): Pass/Fail
- Clear root cause analysis (not just symptom): Pass/Fail
- Concrete, assigned corrective actions with dates: Pass/Fail
- Learnings that change runbooks/process: Pass/Fail
- Stakeholder communication included: Pass/Fail

Game day (exercise) playbook
- Frequency: each service should run a game day annually, SRE-organized. Critical services should run semi-annually.
- Scope: exercises should include KV cache thrashing, autoscaling failure, network partition, and model-serving cold-cache scenarios.
- Pre-game checklist: runbook smoke tested, backups verified, participants and observers assigned, customer comms templates validated.
- Instructor-led script: one-page scenario with expected failure points and scoring rubric.
- Post-exercise retro: 3 actions max with owners and deadlines; update runbooks within 14 days.

Forensics & evidence collection
- What to collect: full request traces (sampled ID list), service logs, autoscaler events, kernel metrics, and model-serving GPU telemetry.
- Retention: preserve a compressed evidence bundle for 90 days in the incident bucket with labels: incident-id, severity, service.

Runbook testing cadence
- Weekly smoke checks for critical-runbooks (automated where possible).
- Quarterly manual validation by rotation lead.
- Annual full-runbook audit by engineering reliability QA.

Customer credits & remediation policy (summary)
- Credits: apply per the customer SLA policy when service-level availability falls below contracted SLA per month. Technical team recommends remediation steps; Customer Success owns credit comms.
- Temporary workaround: rotation lead documents mitigation and timeline; CSM drafts customer message. Legal is looped for enterprise customers before final message if credits are proposed.

Template snippets (copy/paste)
Bridge start message (Slack):
"[BRIDGE] Sev{level} - {service} - {short-impact} - Bridge: {link} - Owner: @{owner} - Next update: +15m"

Public status update:
"Update: Engineers have identified a partial region-level degradation affecting {service}. We have applied temporary throttling and are monitoring. No customer data exposure is suspected. Next update in 15 minutes."

Postmortem action item example: 
- INF-1234: Increase autoscaler cooldown from 30s -> 90s to reduce oscillation. Owner: @alex. ETA: 2026-09-15.

Maintenance: How to retire/update this doc
- Owner (eng rotation lead) must review annually or after every Sev1/2 incident.
- Any runbook changes discovered in postmortem are applied within 14 days and validated by the next rotation.

Appendix: Useful commands and dashboards
- Dashboards: Runtime-Latency, ModelPool-Utilization, Edge-Errors, Redis-Client-Errors
- Useful CLI checks:
  - curl -sS https://health.redwood.internal/v1/ping
  - rtx tail --service serving-runtime --since 5m | jq '.level=="error"'
  - k get hpa -n serving-runtime

Contacts
- Incident mailbox: incidents@redwood.ai
- Pager duty escalation list: pd-sev1@redwood.ai
- Rotation QA: rotations@redwood.ai

Related pages and artifacts
- Maintain runbook links in the team runbook index and ensure the runbook id is on your calendar entry.
